source.title: Unintended memorisation of unique features in neural networks

page_placements.theme: Memorization can retain unique or irrelevant input features

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies memorization of a unique image feature, not fitting randomized training labels, unstructured inputs, label-noise degradation, or the other listed claim versions. Its own results do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on memorizing random training labels, but those cited results are not this study's results. Its own experiments measure unique-feature memorization and related influence effects; these are recorded as findings about a related construct under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures memorisation of a unique visual patch injected into one correctly labelled training image. It does not measure random-label fitting, fitting wholly unstructured inputs, label-noise learning dynamics, or any other specified version. Its discussion of random-label memorisation and real-pattern-first learning cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that single-occurrence visual features can be memorised before overfitting, that tested regularisers do not eliminate this, and that memorisation varies with training seed and architecture. These conclusions concern unique features, not random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study injects one unique visual patch into a single training image and measures sensitivity to that feature using label-confidence or a black-box KL-divergence score; it does not apply the original random-label fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture affect the reported average memorisation scores; the paper reports training-seed variation, and states data augmentation increases memorisation for CNN-2 on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Unique patches can increase their associated label's log-likelihood and model sensitivity. Some canaries have negative scores, and averages in Table 2 include only positive-score canaries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image classifiers can memorise a visual feature appearing in one training image, with variation across canaries and architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Tested regularisers leave positive unique-feature scores. CNN-2's positive-score average rises from 0.018 to 0.13 with augmentation; F-MNIST differences are reported as nonsignificant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout, augmentation, and batch normalisation do not reliably eliminate unique-feature memorisation in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-influence correlates weakly with M for MNIST MLP-1 and not for the other reported datasets. Injecting the patch raises both examined examples' self-influence to 7.5 × 10^4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An example's original self-influence does not adequately explain unique-feature memorisation, and adding a unique feature can increase self-influence.

fits_no_version.finding: The unique patch activates a specific late-layer latent; one canary's sensitivity emerges early, and scores change sign across training seeds for some canaries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unique-feature memorisation can develop early, acquire a latent representation, and depend on training randomness.

record.problems: The measure is an indirect sensitivity score in the black-box setting; results vary with training seed, and the authors note the DenseNet sample size is small. Several seed-variation results are presented in figures without numerical values. Some regularized F-MNIST results are described as not statistically significantly different, without per-condition uncertainty values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the extracted own-result findings selected for this record.

untested.parts: All parts: no completely random training labels or corresponding training/test errors.
All parts: no true-versus-random-label training-time comparison or corruption-dependent convergence.
All parts: no fitting of datasets consisting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian noise. Random comparison patches at inference do not test this.
All parts: no label-corruption sweep or training/test error curves across noise fractions.
All parts: regularisation experiments concern unique-feature sensitivity, not random-label fitting or true-label generalisation after removing regularisation.
All parts: no comparison of shared real-data pattern learning with noisy/random-label memorisation over training.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because their measures address a different construct. This does not negate the reported unique-feature findings. No own result or specific argument tests or refutes the specified versions.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not randomize training labels or report training and test error for random labels.
The study does not compare training time or convergence as label corruption increases.
The study does not train on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The study does not vary the fraction of randomly corrupted labels or report test error across corruption levels.
The study tests regularization against unique-feature memorization, not random-label fitting or generalization on true labels after removing regularization.
The study does not compare learning of real-label patterns with learning of noisy or random labels over training.
